column1: yazi (26.8+): the opener/shell placeholder for ALL selected files' paths — and what replaced the old `"$@"`?
column2:
%s = all selected files' paths. The unified %-family (PR #3232) DEPRECATED the shell-style tokens:
  "$@" (or Windows %*) -> %s   ·   "$0" -> %h   ·   "$N" -> %sN
%* was the OLD WINDOWS token — on Unix it prints literally / does nothing (that's the trap).

column1: yazi %-placeholders: lowercase vs UPPERCASE, and no-suffix vs a number N?
column2:
lowercase = filesystem PATH (%h %s %d), UPPERCASE = URL/file:// (%H %S %D).
no suffix = ALL selected (%s); a number N = just the N-th (%s1, %s2). %h = hovered, %d = dirname,
%% = a literal %. yazi auto-escapes args, so no manual quotes needed.

column1: sed: what do `-n` and the `p` command do, and why are they used together (e.g. `sed -n '/A/,/B/p'`)?
column2:
p = print this line. -n = suppress sed's DEFAULT auto-print of every line. Together: print ONLY the
lines you explicitly p (without -n you'd get every line once + a 2nd copy of matched lines).
'/A/,/B/' is a range address (from a line matching A to the next matching B) → extract that slice.
